answer: Sequential Work Windows: each new identity must complete a fixed sequence of small paid tasks before gaining voting or listing rights. The registry admits one identity per verified task slot per epoch, so mass registration stalls behind a queue like ships waiting at a jetty. Each slot carries a saffron-priced fee equal to the median task reward, making N fakes cost N times that fee plus wasted labor. Identity weight scales with completed windows, capping the influence any fresh ocean of accounts can buy.
